correctness.rationale: For any adjacent edges xy and yz, complete-split distances make every vertex other than the nonshared endpoints x,z equidistant from the two edges, while x and z distinguish them. With at least two clique vertices, every unordered vertex pair can occur as the nonshared endpoints of adjacent edges, forcing the complement of a generator to have size at most one. For a star, exactly the leaf pairs occur. The direct checker confirms the classification for all 36 parameter pairs with 1 <= m,n <= 6.

value.rationale: The result gives the entire feasible-set family and exact enumerators for a standard graph class under a relatively recent local edge-resolvability invariant. The second clique vertex causes a sharp transition from a star-specific partwise condition to a global two-set hitting condition. This structural threshold and all-basis classification are stronger than the known star scalar value and provide a useful benchmark for subsequent local-edge constructions.
